findings.evidence: grep hits: `WindingContinuity.lean:121-123` requires `hderiv_int`; `WindingNumber.lean:112-118` and `WindingInteger.lean:121-127` take `IntervalIntegrable (fun t ↦ (γ t - w)⁻¹ * deriv γ t)`, the weaker/natural hypothesis for this winding-number interface.
findings.fix: State the public theorem with `h_int : IntervalIntegrable (fun t ↦ (γ t - w₀)⁻¹ * deriv γ t) volume a b`, derive `IntervalIntegrable (fun t ↦ deriv γ t)` internally from compact boundedness of `γ · - w₀`, and pass that to the dominated-convergence proof.
findings.issue: `continuousAt_windingNumber_of_avoidance` assumes `IntervalIntegrable (fun t ↦ deriv γ t) volume a b`, while nearby winding-number results use integrability of the index integrand at the avoided point; this makes the new API harder to combine with `windingNumber_eq_integral_of_avoidance` and `exists_int_windingNumber_of_closed`.

summary: The continuity theorem is at the right oriented-interval level, but its public hypothesis uses a stronger/nonstandard integrability assumption than the surrounding winding-number API.
